purpose: Exhibit the divergence between NATQ-001 strict_recall@10 and NATQ-002 case_hit@10 on synthetic fixtures.

cases.why: Aggregation differs: ANY-span passes, ALL-spans fails.

cases.case: SYN-2 single span, chunk filed under a different section_path
cases.why: Match predicate differs: NATQ-001 requires section_path equality, NATQ-002 does not.

cases.case: SYN-3 single span, exact section_path, overlapping chunk
cases.why: Control: the two definitions agree when the case is single-span and the paths match.

cases.case: SYN-4 covering chunk returned below the evaluation depth
cases.why: Control: depth 10 is enforced identically by both.

cases.case: SYN-5 two duplicate covering chunks at ranks 3 and 7
cases.why: Control: duplicates collapse to the best rank in both; no double counting.

cases.case: SYN-6 cross-document case, only the first document's span found
cases.why: Multi-document aggregation: each span resolves in its own version_id under both.

cases.case: SYN-7 one-character overlap at the span boundary
cases.why: Both predicates are half-open interval intersection, so a single shared character hits.

cases_where_strict_and_case_hit_disagree: SYN-2 single span, chunk filed under a different section_path
SYN-6 cross-document case, only the first document's span found
cases_where_strict_and_full_coverage_dis: SYN-2 single span, chunk filed under a different section_path

conclusion.aggregation: strict_recall@10 is an ALL-spans metric; case_hit@10 is an ANY-span metric. SYN-1 and SYN-6 separate them.
conclusion.match_predicate: strict_recall@10 additionally requires section_path equality. SYN-2 separates them.
conclusion.nearest_natq002_analogue_of_strict: case_full_coverage@10 matches the aggregation but still not the predicate; SYN-2 remains a disagreement.
